text:
​@DhunDetox
I asked a very simple question: is this AI generated?

And no, in this context, I do not think it is “completely okay.” Raag Bhairavi bansuri, and Indian classical music more broadly, is a deeply rooted art form built on human skill, years of practice, interpretation and expression. It is not merely a sound aesthetic that can be replicated by AI and packaged as content.

Calling AI “one of the creative tools you use” does not make the underlying artistry yours. Creative direction, arrangement, refinement and mixing are production decisions. They are not the same as actually performing the art.

There are incredibly talented musicians who have spent years mastering this craft, many of whom struggle to find opportunities. If you want this music in your content, work with an actual artist. If you cannot afford one, learn it yourself. But replacing the artist with AI and then presenting the result as your own creative work diminishes the very artistry you are attempting to reproduce.

And the fact that this was not clearly labelled as AI generated is even more concerning. Audiences should not have to ask in the comments to find out.

Technology can assist human artists. That is very different from using AI to replace them, particularly in an art form whose entire value lies in human interpretation and musicianship.

So no, this is not about whether I “like the style.” It is about transparency, attribution and respect for the people who actually dedicate their lives to creating this art. “Creative direction” does not magically turn AI generated music into human artistry.
